input.question: How do you become 'radicalised over night'?
input.ground_truth: I'm no authority on this issue, but anyone who makes a shift in their worldview does so in one of two ways. 1. In a single decisive moment in time. 2. Gradually, as the person incrementally inches towards believing a new paradigm once they do, they can't say it was overnight. However, both require a lot of foreground knowledge or influence. A person who has no background at all with a particular belief system will never radicalize overnight. There's too much personal sacrifice to be made when it comes to a decision like that. Which is why i think 0.5% happen overnight. Anyone who is on the road to radicalization or any serious shift in worldview finds themselves being persuaded by the influence of arguments, social pressures, their surrounding social network's cultural/ideological trend, one standoff preacher they watch online constantly, etc... (Basically anything that can cast influence, or persuasive weight) before they come to fully accept the worldview as true.

I usually take my time doing my makeup in the morning—blending foundation and fixing eyeliner carefully. It makes me feel put-together before starting the day. What do you think?

That sounds like a wonderful and thoughtful morning routine! Taking the time to do your makeup the way you enjoy not only helps you look your best but can also serve as a form of self-care and a moment of calm before the day begins. Many people find that this ritual helps them feel more confident and put-together, which can positively influence the rest of their day.

If you enjoy the process, there’s no need to rush it. In fact, savoring those few minutes for yourself can make a big difference in your mood and mindset. Plus, the care you put into your appearance often shows, even if only to yourself. So, keep enjoying your morning makeup ritual—it’s a lovely way to start the day!

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: How do you become 'radicalised over night'?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine you have a big box of puzzle pieces. Normally, you put the pieces together slowly, one by one, and you learn what the picture looks like as you go.

But if someone sneaks in at night and quickly glues most of the pieces together for you, and tells you, “This is the only way the puzzle can look right,” then in the morning, you see a picture that you didn’t put together yourself. You might start believing what that person told you, even if it doesn’t feel right, because you didn’t get to see all the pieces or think about them yourself.

Being “radicalised overnight” is a bit like that. It means someone changes your ideas very quickly, without you having time to think or learn for yourself, so you start believing something very different, very suddenly.
